newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - China Investment Bank borrows.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - China Investment Bank borrows.

text.p: China Investment Bank on Thursday became the latest Chinese issuer to introduce a floating rate note issue to Asian debt markets and, like its recent predecessors, the note received a warm welcome.
"The issue has been trading pretty well and there's been some distribution in Europe as well as in Asia," said a syndicate manager involved with the deal.
The $100 million FRN matures in five years and was launched and re-offered at par to float at 45 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
Fees are 35 basis points to give an all-in return of 53 basis points.
Bayerische Landesbank Hong Kong branch and Chase Manhattan Asia are lead managers and bookrunners. Daiwa Securities Hong Kong, HSBC Markets and Standard Chartered Bank also acted as lead managers.
The deal was bid at 99.95 and offered at 100.05 after it was freed to trade in the afternoon, bankers said.
China Investment Bank is majority owned by China Construction Bank, which had its own $200 million FRN in the market a few weeks ago.
That deal also attracted a wide following.
With financial troubles in South Korea and Thailand putting a damper on issuance from these countries, investors have increasingly turned to China for new paper.

Beijing's China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) is expected to be the next Chinese entity to tap the FRN market. Agricultural Bank of China also is widely rumoured to be pondering an FRN.
Hong Kong dollar deals also were in the news.
Bookrunner Societe Generale Asia said it was seeking an arranger group for Bank of East Asia's three-year HK$2.5 billion floating rate certificate of deposit.
Application will be made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the certificates as eligible for use at its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Malaysia's Public Bank has mandated five banks to arrange a three-year HK$1.0 billion FRCD pending government approval.
